title: Capacity Orchestra: SLO-backed scaling macros and provenance logbook in Console
creator: Liam Chen
description: Add a new Console 'Capacity Orchestra' surface that combines (1) SLO-backed scaling macros — named, parameterized autoscale recipes that guarantee throughput targets for a fleet or route; (2) an interactive throughput dashboard that shows live vs. guaranteed capacity, estimated headroom, and forecasted drop probability; and (3) a provenance logbook that captures who changed capacity policies, the pre/post telemetry snapshot, and an easy rollback to any prior configuration. The goal is to give operators clear, auditable controls for Dedicated capacity guarantees while reducing manual intervention during traffic spikes.

acceptance_criteria: Console shows 'Capacity Orchestra' entry under Fleet Controls with access controlled by RBAC role: fleet-operator
Operators can create, name, and edit a scaling macro with params: target_throughput, min_replicas, max_replicas, cool_down_secs, preempt_policy
Each macro can be simulated against last 7 days of telemetry and returns projected p95 latency, projected token/sec headroom, and a confidence score
Apply-macro action triggers an atomic policy update and records a provenance snapshot including user, timestamp, config diff, and condensed telemetry summary
Provenance logbook supports filtering by user, fleet, and date and allows rollback to any logged policy with a single click and a required confirmation modal
Throughput dashboard displays live vs. guaranteed throughput, short-term forecast (1h), drop probability, and a recommended macro when guarantees are at risk
Backend endpoints are covered by unit and integration tests and a load test validating apply-macro latency under 200ms median for single-fleet calls
Security review completed and RBAC + audit headers validated in staging
decisions: Store telemetry snapshots as condensed summaries (quantiles + recent histogram) rather than full traces to control cost
Confidence score derived from recent pattern-matching algorithm (last 14d) rather than a black-box ML model for explainability
Enable only soft guarantees for first rollout (alerting + routing fallback) and require ops approval to flip to hard preemptive guarantees
Expose 'simulate' as a non-mutating dry-run API that returns deterministic results based on stored snapshots
